value.headline: Democrats build massive vote-by-mail advantage in New Jersey, outpacing 2025 returns
value.claim: D share of returned VBM 66.7% vs 63% at the same point in 2025; D lead 152,000+
value.evidence: Numbers check against UF/NJ SOS [R]. But the like-for-like midterm (2022) VBM split was D65-R20 late in the count [R], close to 2026 D65.5-R18.9 at day 11 [R]; vs 2024 day 13 (D61.6-R20.5, D+41.1) 2026 is about 5 pts more D. In 2025 the mail split was D+40.6 at this point and Sherrill won by 14.4 [R], so the mail split is a weak predictor of the margin.

rows.source: New Jersey Globe (UMichVoter data): Democrats build massive vote-by-mail advantage in New Jersey, outpacing 2025 ret
rows.note: The verdict is our like-for-like reading of the claim (grade I); the evidence cites its own grades.

value.headline: Democrats dominate early vote-by-mail returns in New Jersey, including three key congressional districts
value.claim: Democrats are 66% of 364,128 returned VBMs; D leads in NJ-7 (60-23), NJ-2 (59-27), NJ-9 (66-18)
value.cmp: none in the headline; article itself warns Republicans rely on Election Day
value.evidence: Counts match later UF/NJ SOS series [R]. Like-for-like: NJ-7 VBM D+36 at day 15 vs D+33 at day 15 in 2022 (Kean won by 2.8) and D+30 in 2024 (Kean won by 5.4) [R/M]. In 2024 Republicans then led NJ-7 in-person early voting 46-30 [R].

value.headline: Early Voting Opens Saturday in NJ With Democrats Ahead in Mail Ballots
value.claim: "the mail figures lack a baseline for comparison"; early returns do not yet show the wave visible in polls
value.evidence: A baseline exists: AP researcher Ryan Dubicki published same-point counts for 2022 and 2024 (NJ Globe). 2026 VBM is more D than 2024 (D+46.6 at day 11 vs D+41.1 at day 13) and about level with 2022 [R/M]. Cassino is right that mail alone cannot show a wave: volume at day 15 is 364k vs 321k (2022) and 471k (2024) [R].
